claim: Switching threshold and output logic levels of the sky130 single-ended D+ and D- receivers under local device mismatch (Monte Carlo, vary=mismatch, `*_mm` library sections) at tt (27 C, 3.3 V) and at the binding corner of the 45-point records (ff, 100 C, 3.0 V), against spec/usb2-phy.md section 6 row 'Single-ended receiver thresholds' VIH > 2.0 V, VIL < 0.8 V, read as in docs/porting-plan.md and the deterministic records (threshold strictly inside (0.8 V, 2.0 V), output a valid logic level below 0.8 V and above 2.0 V). Schematic-level, no layout parasitics; not a signoff or catalog-tier claim.

record.netlist_provenance: schematic-derived netlists: xschem export of design/se_receiver_dp.sch and design/se_receiver_dm.sch (design/netlist/se_receiver_{dp,dm}.spice) plus the Monte Carlo testbench decks, frozen per campaign; no layout, no parasitic extraction
record.statistical_convention: Monte Carlo of local device mismatch only (monte_carlo.vary = mismatch): n = 400 samples per corner per receiver, base seed 166, per-sample seeds derived by `klt sim`; every MOS and res_xhigh_po_1p41 instance (R1, R2, RBIAS and the comparator devices) draws independent mismatch (mc_mm_switch = 1 through the `*_mm` library sections); global process spread is the separate corner axis and is not sampled
method: Stimulus and measurements as sim/se-receiver-dp-thresholds and sim/se-receiver-dm-thresholds: the line input swept 0 - 3.0 V at 1 mV; supply, temperature and library section of the corner.

Row measurements: `vth_v` = first rising crossing of RXD through VDD/2, must lie strictly inside (0.8 V, 2.0 V); `rxd_low_max_v` = maximum of RXD over input 0 - 0.8 V, must be <= 0.1 x VDD; `rxd_high_min_v` = minimum of RXD over input 2.0 - 3.0 V, must be >= 0.9 x VDD. A sample with no rising crossing (an inverted or dead receiver) has no `vth_v` and is reported by klt yield as `errored`; the lint requires errored = 0 for a PASS record.

Each (receiver, corner) is its own population: one `klt sim` Monte Carlo request, backend batch, per receiver per corner; nothing is pooled across corners or across D+/D-. `klt yield-samples` pairs each nominal campaign with its negative-control campaign (same deck, same seeds, the deterministic skew below), and `klt yield` grades the pair against the row limits with target_yield 0.99 at 95 % confidence.

Negative control (deterministic): the control campaign lengthens R2 from 14 to 60 (fixed divider-ratio skew), which moves VREF and so the threshold above 2.0 V at every sample. The yield report must flag it `detected` for every measurement that the skew degrades (at least `vth_v`); a campaign whose control is `not_detected` for `vth_v` cannot be a PASS record.

Mismatch activity: as in sim/diff-receiver-mismatch; the stddev of `vth_v` in each yield report's `distribution` is the evidence that mismatch reached the divider and the comparator (a stddev of zero would fail the record).
PDK: the pinned open_pdks revision of sim/pdk-pins.json (current pin); each record states the revision and the model library sha256.
record.footer: Scope: schematic-level statistical evidence for one block against the ratified single-ended-threshold row, at the corners named in the record. Local device mismatch only; global process spread is covered by the deterministic corner records, and the corner x mismatch combination is limited to the two corners named. It does not claim layout, DRC/LVS, input hysteresis, level shifting or signoff, and does not relax any target. A FAIL record is evidence of failure, not compliance.

yield.sample_size_justification: target_yield 0.99 at 95 % two-sided confidence: with zero observed failures the exact (Clopper-Pearson) lower bound reaches 0.99 only for n >= 368 (klt yield `required_n_for_target`), so n = 400 per corner is the smallest round count that can support the claim; the +/-0.01 precision target needs n >= 183. A failing row is not rescued by a larger n: it is recorded as failing.
